--- title: "[GAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Generalized Additive Model with automatic smoothness selection. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L174-L1841){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python GAM(formula, family=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A GAM extends the generalized linear model by replacing some or all linear predictor terms with smooth, data-driven functions of the covariates: $$ g(\mathbb{E}[y_i]) = \eta_i = \beta_0 + \sum_j \beta_j x_{ij} + \sum_k f_k(z_{ik}) $$ where $g$ is a link function, $\beta_j x_{ij}$ are ordinary parametric (linear) terms, and each $f_k$ is an unspecified smooth function represented by a spline basis (`s()`) or a tensor product of bases for multivariate smooths (`te()`, `ti()`, `t2()`). This lets the model capture nonlinear relationships without having to guess a parametric form ahead of time, while still supporting the full range of exponential-family response distributions (Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma, Tweedie, and more) via a `Family` object. Use `GAM` when you suspect a covariate's effect on the response is nonlinear, when you want interaction surfaces between two or more continuous covariates, or when you want automatic, data-driven control of model complexity rather than manually choosing a polynomial degree or a fixed set of basis functions. A `GAM` is specified with a formula string in an R/mgcv-like syntax, e.g. `"y ~ s(x1) + s(x2, bs='cr', k=15) + te(x3, x4) + group"`, where `s()` denotes a univariate (or `by=`-varying) smooth, `te()`/`ti()`/`t2()` denote tensor-product smooths of two or more variables, and bare names denote ordinary parametric terms. See `Formula`, `SmoothTerm`, `LinearTerm`, `InteractionTerm`, and `OffsetTerm` for the term types this formula parses into. Fitting (`fit()`) proceeds by Penalized Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (P-IRLS): each smooth's wiggliness is controlled by a quadratic penalty $\lambda_k \boldsymbol{\beta}_k^T \mathbf{S}_k \boldsymbol{\beta}_k$ on its coefficients, and the smoothing parameters $\lambda_k$ are themselves estimated from the data. By default this is via Generalized Cross-Validation (GCV), or via Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) or Marginal Likelihood (ML) when smooths are treated as correlated random effects. Larger $\lambda_k$ shrinks a smooth toward a simpler (e.g. linear or constant) shape; smaller $\lambda_k$ allows more flexibility. This automatic selection is what distinguishes a GAM from simply choosing a fixed spline basis: the *effective* complexity of each term (its effective degrees of freedom, or EDF) is learned rather than fixed in advance. Once fitted, a `GAM` supports prediction with standard errors and intervals (`predict()`), partial-effect plotting (`plot()`), residual and basis-dimension diagnostics (`check()`, `gam_check()`, `k_check()`), hypothesis tests for parametric and smooth terms (`parametric_tests()`, `smooth_tests()`), and a text summary (`summary()`) analogous to `summary.gam()` in R's mgcv. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str or Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Model formula, either as a string (e.g. `"y ~ s(x1) + s(x2) + x3"`) or an already-parsed `Formula` object. The left-hand side names the response column; the right-hand side lists smooth terms (`s()`, `te()`, `ti()`, `t2()`), parametric terms (bare column names), interactions (`x1 * x2`), and optionally an `offset(...)` term. Use `0 +` or `- 1` on the right-hand side to suppress the intercept. [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Response distribution and link function. Defaults to `Gaussian()` (identity link) if not given. Other options include `Binomial`, `Poisson`, `Gamma`, and `Tweedie`-family classes, each defining the variance function, deviance, and link used during P-IRLS. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#4c8cc39e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker import GAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) x = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, 10, 200)) y = np.sin(x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=200) gam = GAM("y ~ s(x)").fit({"x": x, "y": y}) print(gam.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Gaussian(link='identity') Inference: GCV Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err t value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.1325 0.0146 9.073 1.441e-16 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 8.35 9 1996.690 < 1e-16 Total EDF: 9.35 Scale est: 0.042647 Deviance: 8.1308 Null dev: 93.9889 Dev. expl: 91.3% GCV score: 0.044739 AIC: -54.03 BIC: -23.20 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
aic Akaike Information Criterion of the fitted model.
bic Bayesian Information Criterion of the fitted model.
coefficients Estimated coefficients $\boldsymbol{\beta}$.
deviance Model deviance at convergence.
deviance_explained Proportion of null deviance explained by the model (analogous to R²).
edf Effective degrees of freedom (EDF) for each smooth term.
edf_total Total effective degrees of freedom across all model terms.
family The response distribution family used to fit this model.
fitted_values Fitted values $\mu$ on the response scale.
formula The parsed model formula.
gcv_score Generalized Cross-Validation score at the fitted smoothing parameters.
is_fitted Whether the model has been fitted.
mcmc_result The `MCMCResult` when the model was fitted with `method="MCMC"`, else `None`.
null_deviance Deviance of the intercept-only (null) model.
residuals Response residuals ($y - \mu$) on the training data.
scale Estimated scale (dispersion) parameter $\phi$.
smoothing_params Selected or fixed smoothing parameters $\lambda_j$, one per penalty.
vi_result The `VIResult` when the model was fitted with `method="VI"`, else `None`.
### [aic]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Akaike Information Criterion of the fitted model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [aic]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Balances goodness of fit against model complexity (using the total effective degrees of freedom in place of the raw parameter count). Lower values indicate a preferable trade-off; use it to compare non-nested models fitted to the same data and family. ::: ### [bic]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Bayesian Information Criterion of the fitted model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [bic]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Like `aic`, but penalizes model complexity more heavily as sample size grows (using `log(n)` in place of `2` as the per-degree-of-freedom penalty), which tends to favor simpler models than AIC for larger datasets. ::: ### [coefficients]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Estimated coefficients $\boldsymbol{\beta}$. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [coefficients]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} A single flat vector holding the intercept, parametric term coefficients, and every smooth term's basis coefficients concatenated in formula order. Use `self._model_matrix.smooths` (or `predict(type="terms")`) to map sub-ranges of this vector back to individual terms. ::: ### [deviance]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Model deviance at convergence. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [deviance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Twice the difference between the saturated log-likelihood and the fitted model's log-likelihood, evaluated at the final coefficients. Lower values indicate a better fit to the training data; compare against `null_deviance` via `deviance_explained`. ::: ### [deviance_explained]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Proportion of null deviance explained by the model (analogous to R²). ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [deviance_explained]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computed as `1 - deviance / null_deviance`. Ranges from `0` (no improvement over an intercept-only model) up to `1` (a perfect fit), and provides a family-agnostic measure of goodness of fit that generalizes R² beyond the Gaussian case. ::: ### [edf]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Effective degrees of freedom (EDF) for each smooth term. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [edf]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each value is the trace of the portion of the hat matrix attributable to that term, reflecting how much shrinkage its smoothing parameter applied: values near the term's basis dimension indicate little penalization, values near 1 indicate near-linear shrinkage. ::: ### [edf_total]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Total effective degrees of freedom across all model terms. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [edf_total]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} The sum of the per-term EDF values (plus the intercept and parametric terms), i.e. the trace of the full hat (influence) matrix. Used in `summary()`, `gam_check()`, and in computing residual degrees of freedom for interval and test calculations. ::: ### [family]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The response distribution family used to fit this model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Determines the variance function, deviance, and link function used during P-IRLS. Defaults to `Gaussian()` when no `family` argument was given to `GAM.__init__()`. ::: ### [fitted_values]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Fitted values $\mu$ on the response scale. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [fitted_values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Equal to $g^{-1}(\eta)$ where $\eta = \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the linear predictor evaluated on the training data used in `fit()`. ::: ### [formula]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The parsed model formula. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the `Formula` object produced by parsing the formula string passed to `GAM.__init__()` (or the `Formula` object passed directly). It lists the response column and the parsed smooth (`s()`, `te()`, `ti()`, `t2()`), parametric, interaction, and offset terms that make up the right-hand side. ::: ### [gcv_score]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Generalized Cross-Validation score at the fitted smoothing parameters. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [gcv_score]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computed as $\text{GCV} = n \cdot D / (n - \text{tr}(\mathbf{H}))^2$, where $D$ is the deviance and $\mathbf{H}$ is the hat matrix. This is the criterion minimized when `fit(method="GCV")` selects smoothing parameters, and is reported even when a different `method` was used. ::: ### [is_fitted]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the model has been fitted. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_fitted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} `True` once `fit()` has completed successfully; `False` beforehand. Most other properties and methods (`coefficients`, `predict()`, `summary()`, etc.) require this to be `True` and raise a `RuntimeError` via `_check_fitted()` otherwise. ::: ### [mcmc_result]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The `MCMCResult` when the model was fitted with `method="MCMC"`, else `None`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [mcmc_result]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [MCMCResult | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [null_deviance]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Deviance of the intercept-only (null) model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [null_deviance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fit on the same data and with the same family and weights, but with every covariate effect (smooth and parametric) removed. Serves as the baseline against which `deviance_explained` measures the reduction in deviance achieved by the fitted model. ::: ### [residuals]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Response residuals ($y - \mu$) on the training data. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [residuals]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} These are the raw (unstandardized) residuals. For Pearson, deviance, or working residuals (or residuals on new data) use `get_residuals()` instead. ::: ### [scale]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Estimated scale (dispersion) parameter $\phi$. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} For families with a known scale (Binomial, Poisson) this is fixed at `1.0`. For families with unknown scale (Gaussian, Gamma, Tweedie) it is estimated from the Pearson residuals and is used to scale coefficient standard errors and prediction intervals. ::: ### [smoothing_params]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Selected or fixed smoothing parameters $\lambda_j$, one per penalty. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [smoothing_params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} If `fit()` was called with `smoothing_params=None` (the default), these are the values chosen automatically via GCV, REML, or ML; otherwise they are the fixed values that were passed in. A `te()`/`t2()` term contributes more than one entry (one per marginal penalty), so this list is generally longer than the number of smooth terms. ::: ### [vi_result]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The `VIResult` when the model was fitted with `method="VI"`, else `None`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [vi_result]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [VIResult | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
anova() Compare this model with one or more other fitted GAMs via deviance-difference tests.
concurvity() Compute concurvity diagnostics for all smooth terms.
derivatives() Estimate derivatives of smooth terms with respect to a variable.
dispersion_test() Test for overdispersion in Poisson or Binomial models.
fit() Fit the GAM to data via Penalized Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (P-IRLS).
gam_check() Run all-in-one GAM diagnostics.
get_residuals() Compute residuals of the specified type.
influence() Compute hat values and Cook's distance for each observation.
k_check() Check basis dimension adequacy for each smooth term.
marginal_effects() Compute marginal (partial) effects of a variable.
pairwise_comparisons() Compute pairwise contrasts between conditions.
parametric_tests() Compute Wald tests for parametric (non-smooth) coefficients.
plot() Plot the estimated partial effect of each smooth term, with a confidence band.
posterior_samples() Draw coefficient vectors from the posterior.
predict() Predict from the fitted model on new data.
quantile_residuals() Compute randomized quantile residuals (Dunn & Smyth 1996).
simulate() Draw from the posterior distribution of the fitted model.
simultaneous_ci() Compute simultaneous confidence bands for smooth terms.
smooth_tests() Compute approximate p-values for all smooth terms.
summary() Return a text summary of the fitted model, analogous to `summary.gam()` in R's mgcv.
vif() Compute variance inflation factors for parametric (linear) terms.
### [anova()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compare this model with one or more other fitted GAMs via deviance-difference tests. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1429-L1459){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python anova(*others) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} All models must use the same family and be fitted to the same data. Models are automatically sorted by complexity (edf). For known-scale families (Poisson, Binomial) a chi-squared test is used. For unknown-scale families (Gaussian, Gamma) an F-test is used. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [*others]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [GAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One or more fitted `GAM` objects to compare against this model. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [AnovaResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sequential deviance-comparison table. ::: ### [concurvity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute concurvity diagnostics for all smooth terms. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1407-L1427){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python concurvity(*, full=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Concurvity is the GAM analogue of collinearity. High values (> 0.8) indicate that a smooth's effect may be confounded with other model terms, making its estimate unstable. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [full]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), measure each smooth against all other model terms combined. If `False`, compute pairwise concurvity between each pair of smooths. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ConcurvityResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Object with `worst`, `observed`, and `estimate` arrays, plus `labels`. ::: ### [derivatives()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Estimate derivatives of smooth terms with respect to a variable. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1681-L1730){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python derivatives( variable, *, order=1, n_points=200, level=0.95, eps=None, unconditional=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses central finite differences on the basis matrix with delta-method standard errors. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [variable]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The covariate to differentiate with respect to. [order]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Derivative order: `1` for first derivative (rate of change), `2` for second derivative (curvature). [n_points]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of evaluation points along the variable's range. [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the bands. [eps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Finite difference step size. If `None`, chosen automatically. [unconditional]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use unconditional covariance (Marra & Wood 2012). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[DerivativeResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per smooth term involving the variable. ::: ### [dispersion_test()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Test for overdispersion in Poisson or Binomial models. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1655-L1666){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python dispersion_test() ``` ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DispersionTestResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Object with `dispersion`, `chi2_stat`, and `p_value`. ::: ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the GAM to data via Penalized Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (P-IRLS). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L309-L433){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit( data, *, smoothing_params=None, method="GCV", weights=None, select=False, vi_options=None, mcmc_options=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Builds the model matrix from the formula, then alternates between (a) an IRLS step that linearizes the exponential-family log-likelihood around the current fit and (b) a penalized weighted-least-squares solve that shrinks each smooth toward simplicity according to its smoothing parameter. When `smoothing_params` is not fixed, this inner P-IRLS loop is itself wrapped in an outer loop that re-estimates the smoothing parameters (by GCV, REML, or ML) at each iteration, until both the coefficients and the smoothing parameters converge. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, numpy.ndarray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented data as `{name: 1-D array}`. All columns referenced by the formula (response, smooth covariates, parametric terms, and any `by=` factor) must be present. [smoothing_params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float] or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fixed smoothing parameters $\lambda_k$, one per penalty (a `te()`/`t2()` term contributes more than one). If `None` (default), smoothing parameters are selected automatically via `method`. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["GCV"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Criterion used to select smoothing parameters when `smoothing_params` is not fixed. One of: - `"GCV"` (default): minimizes the Generalized Cross-Validation score $\text{GCV} = n \cdot D / (n - \text{tr}(\mathbf{H}))^2$, where $D$ is the deviance and $\mathbf{H}$ is the influence (hat) matrix. Fast and does not require treating smooths as random effects, but can occasionally undersmooth. - `"REML"`: maximizes the Restricted Maximum Likelihood, treating each smooth's penalized coefficients as correlated Gaussian random effects and integrating out the fixed (unpenalized) effects. Generally the most reliable choice and the one recommended when using `select=True`. - `"ML"`: maximizes the Marginal Likelihood, similar to REML but without correcting for uncertainty in the fixed effects; tends to undersmooth slightly relative to REML. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [numpy.ndarray or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Observation (prior) weights, shape `(n,)`. Must be positive. When provided, the model minimizes the weighted deviance $\sum_i w_i d_i$ and uses weighted IRLS throughout. [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, augment each smooth's wiggliness penalty with a second penalty on its null space (the component, such as a pure linear trend, that the ordinary penalty never shrinks). With both penalties free, GCV/REML/ML can drive a term's smoothing parameters high enough to remove it from the model entirely, giving automatic term selection analogous to the lasso (Marra & Wood, 2011). Recommended together with `method="REML"`. Has no additional effect on bases whose null space is already zero (e.g. `bs="re"`, `bs="fs"`, or the shrinkage bases `"ts"`/`"cs"`). [vi_options]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Extra keyword arguments forwarded to `~whittaker.fitting.vi.vi_fit` when `method="VI"`. Accepted keys: `n_quad`, `lr`, `max_iter`, `tol`, `patience`, `seed`, `cov_structure`, `phi_inference`. Ignored for all other methods. [mcmc_options]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Extra keyword arguments forwarded to `~whittaker.fitting.mcmc.mcmc_fit` when `method="MCMC"`. Accepted keys: `n_samples`, `n_warmup`, `n_chains`, `leapfrog_steps`, `target_accept`, `seed`. Ignored for all other methods. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [GAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining, e.g. `GAM(formula).fit(data).predict(new_data)`. ::: ### [gam_check()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Run all-in-one GAM diagnostics. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1292-L1319){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python gam_check(*, n_sim=100) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a `GamCheckResult` containing deviance residuals, fitted values, response values, basis dimension checks, and summary statistics. Print the result for a quick diagnostic summary. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_sim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each smooth, computes a k-index based on the ratio of a neighbor-differencing variance estimate of the residuals (ordered by covariate) to the overall residual variance. A simulation-based p-value is computed: low p-values indicate potential under-smoothing. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_sim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[400]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of random permutations for the p-value simulation (default `400`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[KCheckResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per smooth term. ::: ### [marginal_effects()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute marginal (partial) effects of a variable. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1732-L1778){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python marginal_effects( variable, *, at=None, n_points=200, level=0.95, unconditional=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Evaluates the smooth term(s) involving *variable* over a grid while holding other variables at their means or at values specified via *at*. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [variable]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The focal covariate. [at]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Dict mapping other variable names to fixed values (or lists of values for a grid). Variables not listed are held at their mean. [n_points]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of evaluation points along the variable's range. [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the bands. [unconditional]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use unconditional covariance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[MarginalEffectResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per smooth term per `at` combination. ::: ### [pairwise_comparisons()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute pairwise contrasts between conditions. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1780-L1825){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python pairwise_comparisons( variable, pairs, *, n_points=200, level=0.95, unconditional=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each pair is `(condition1, condition2)` where each condition is a dict of covariate values. The contrast `f(x|cond1) - f(x|cond2)` is evaluated over a grid of the focal variable. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [variable]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The focal covariate (the x-axis for the contrast). [pairs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[dict, dict]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of `(cond1, cond2)` dicts specifying the two conditions. [n_points]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of evaluation points. [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the bands. [unconditional]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use unconditional covariance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[ContrastResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per smooth term per pair. ::: ### [parametric_tests()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute Wald tests for parametric (non-smooth) coefficients. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1232-L1248){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python parametric_tests() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses the t-distribution for families with unknown scale (Gaussian, Gamma) and the z-distribution for known-scale families (Binomial, Poisson). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[ParametricTestResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per parametric coefficient (intercept + linear terms). ::: ### [plot()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Plot the estimated partial effect of each smooth term, with a confidence band. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1573-L1618){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python plot(*, n_points=200, level=0.95) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For every smooth in the formula, evaluates the term's contribution to the linear predictor over an evenly spaced grid spanning its covariate's observed range (holding other terms out, i.e., this shows the additive component `f_k(x)` itself, not the full fitted response), together with a pointwise confidence band derived from the model's coefficient covariance. This is the standard way to visually inspect the *shape* of each estimated smooth (e.g., whether it is roughly linear, monotonic, or has a distinct peak) without needing to call `predict(type="terms")` and plot manually. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_points]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of evenly spaced evaluation points per smooth (the default is `200`). [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the bands, e.g. `0.95` for a 95% band (the default is `0.95`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [altair.VConcatChart or altair.Chart]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A vertically concatenated chart with one panel per smooth term (or a single `Chart` if the model has exactly one smooth). ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#0a6de81d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker import GAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) x = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, 10, 200)) y = np.sin(x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=200) gam = GAM("y ~ s(x)").fit({"x": x, "y": y}) gam.plot() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### [posterior_samples()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Draw coefficient vectors from the posterior. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1192-L1230){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python posterior_samples(n=1000, *, seed=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For VI fits, samples from the variational posterior `N(m, C)`. For Laplace fits (REML/GCV/ML), samples from `N(β̂, V_β)`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of draws. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Shape `(p, n)`, where `p` is the number of model coefficients. ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict from the fitted model on new data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L483-L646){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict( new_data, *, se=False, type="response", interval=None, level=0.95, unconditional=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies the estimated coefficients to a model matrix built from `new_data`, using the same basis transformations (knots, factor levels, centering constraints) fitted on the training data. Supports predictions on the response or linear-predictor scale, per-term decompositions, and pointwise or simultaneous uncertainty intervals. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, numpy.ndarray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented new data. Must contain all covariate columns referenced by the formula (the response column is not needed). [se]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, compute standard errors on the linear predictor scale (for `type="response"` and `type="link"`) or per-term standard errors (for `type="terms"`). Default `False`. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["response"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Prediction type. One of: - `"response"` (default): predictions on the response scale, $\mu = g^{-1}(\eta)$. - `"link"`: predictions on the linear predictor scale, $\eta = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta}$. - `"terms"`: individual smooth term contributions to the linear predictor, returned separately rather than summed (see `TermsPredictionResult`). [interval]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Interval type. `None` (default) returns no intervals. Ignored (and must be `None`) when `type="terms"`. Otherwise one of: - `"confidence"`: interval for the mean response, reflecting uncertainty in $\eta$ only. - `"prediction"`: interval for a new individual observation, adding the response-distribution variance on top of the uncertainty in $\eta$. - `"simultaneous"`: a band with `level` coverage for the *entire* curve simultaneously (via posterior simulation), rather than pointwise coverage. All interval types are computed on the linear predictor scale and transformed to the response scale for `type="response"`. [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Nominal coverage probability for the interval, e.g. `0.95` for a 95% interval (default). [unconditional]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, include smoothing-parameter uncertainty in standard errors and intervals (Marra & Wood, 2012), using the unconditional covariance matrix $V_c$ in place of the conditional $V_p$. This produces wider, more honest intervals that account for the fact that $\lambda$ was itself estimated from the data. Requires that the model was fitted with `method="REML"` or `method="ML"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [PredictionResult or TermsPredictionResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For `type="response"` or `type="link"`, a `PredictionResult` with `values`, `se`, `linear_predictor`, `lower`, and `upper`. For `type="terms"`, a `TermsPredictionResult` with per-smooth contributions and standard errors. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#ca74b851 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker import GAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) x = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, 10, 200)) y = np.sin(x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=200) gam = GAM("y ~ s(x)").fit({"x": x, "y": y}) new_x = np.linspace(0, 10, 5) result = gam.predict({"x": new_x}, se=True, interval="confidence") result.values, result.lower, result.upper ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display -0.96003228, 1.001784 , -0.42504195])) ``` ::: ::: ### [quantile_residuals()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute randomized quantile residuals (Dunn & Smyth 1996). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1633-L1653){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python quantile_residuals(*, seed=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For a correctly specified model, these should be approximately standard normal. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the jittering step (discrete families). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Quantile residuals, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Draw from the posterior distribution of the fitted model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1321-L1405){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(new_data=None, *, n_sim=1000, seed=None, unconditional=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Generates posterior simulations of the response by: 1. Drawing coefficient vectors β* ~ MVN(β̂, V_β) from the Bayesian posterior. 2. Computing η* = X @ β* (+ offset if present) for each draw. 3. Transforming to the response scale: μ* = g⁻¹(η*). When `unconditional=True`, response noise is added by sampling from the family distribution at each μ*. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column-oriented data for prediction. If `None`, uses the training data. [n_sim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of posterior draws (default `1000`). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. [unconditional]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, add response-distribution noise on top of posterior uncertainty in the mean. This produces simulations of new observations rather than of the conditional mean. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated values on the response scale, shape `(n, n_sim)` where `n` is the number of observations in the prediction data. ::: ### [simultaneous_ci()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute simultaneous confidence bands for smooth terms. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L822-L911){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simultaneous_ci( new_data, *, term=None, level=0.95, n_sim=10000, unconditional=False, seed=0 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Unlike pointwise intervals, these bands have (approximate) `level=` coverage probability for the *entire* function simultaneously, not just at individual points. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Prediction data. [term]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which smooth term to compute bands for. An integer index (0-based) or the term label string. If `None` and the model has exactly one smooth, that term is used. [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Nominal simultaneous coverage probability (default `0.95`). [n_sim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of posterior simulations for the critical value (default `10_000`). [unconditional]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, include smoothing parameter uncertainty. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Keys: `"estimate"`, `"se"`, `"lower"`, `"upper"`, `"term_label"`, `"crit_value"`. ::: ### [smooth_tests()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute approximate p-values for all smooth terms. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1250-L1264){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python smooth_tests() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses the Wood (2013) approach: eigendecomposition of the Bayesian covariance block for each smooth, with a chi-squared reference distribution. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[SmoothTestResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per smooth term. ::: ### [summary()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return a text summary of the fitted model, analogous to `summary.gam()` in R's mgcv. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1461-L1571){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python summary() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The summary reports, in order: the formula and family; a table of parametric (non-smooth) coefficients with estimates, standard errors, test statistics (`t` for unknown-scale families such as Gaussian and Gamma, `z` for known-scale families such as Binomial and Poisson), and p-values; a table of approximate significance for each smooth term (effective degrees of freedom, reference degrees of freedom, a chi-squared-type statistic, and a p-value); and overall fit statistics (total EDF, deviance, null deviance, proportion of deviance explained, GCV score, estimated scale, AIC, and BIC). Use this for a quick, human-readable check of which terms are significant and how well the model fits, without extracting individual result objects via `parametric_tests()` and `smooth_tests()`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ModelSummary]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Multi-line text summary. Displays cleanly as the last expression in a Jupyter or Quarto cell without needing `print()`. ::: ### [vif()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute variance inflation factors for parametric (linear) terms. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/gam.py#L1668-L1679){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vif() ``` ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[VIFResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One result per parametric term. Empty if fewer than 2 parametric terms. :::
